items.title: Palo Alto confirms limited attacks on a PAN-OS management-interface RCE; CISA sets Oct 17 deadline
items.summary: An authenticated attacker who can reach the PAN-OS management interface can run code as root on PA-Series and VM-Series firewalls and on Panorama; Cloud NGFW and Prisma Access are not affected. Palo Alto reports very limited exploitation and lists three source IPs (66.42.72[.]14, 208.83.239[.]114, 149.248.47[.]234), and CISA has added the bug to KEV. Upgrade to the fixed hotfix for your train (e.g. 12.2.4, 11.2.16, 11.1.16-h3, 10.2.18-h12) and lock the management interface down to trusted internal hosts or a jump box.

items.title: Cisco Secure Email Gateway bug lets a crafted attachment write files and run commands as root, now exploited
items.summary: A path traversal in the AMP File Reputation feature of Cisco Secure Email Gateway lets an unauthenticated sender plant files and gain root via an email attachment; it is exploitable when File Reputation is on in a mail policy and Content Scanner Tools is below 25.3.0.5525. Cisco confirms active attacks and there is no workaround. Update Content Scanner Tools to 25.3.0.5525+ or move to AsyncOS 15.5.5-014 / 16.5.0-780, and check external firewall logs for odd outbound uploads, since root access lets attackers wipe local evidence.

items.title: Exploited AhsayCBS auth-bypass and command-injection chain gets new hotfixes after earlier patches fell short
items.summary: Attackers are chaining an authentication bypass and a command injection in the AhsayCBS backup server to get unauthenticated code execution, dropping web shells and XMRig miners, according to Huntress. The August builds 9.15.2.59 and 10.3.4.0 did not fully close the hole, and CISA has put both CVEs in KEV with an Oct 17 deadline. Install hotfix 10.3.4.45 or 9.15.2.70, reboot, and hunt for web shells and miners on any internet-facing server.

items.title: Next.js out-of-band release fixes two critical RCE paths in 'use cache' and SVG handling via sharp
items.summary: Next.js 16.4.1 and 15.5.28 fix a code-execution bug in App Router apps that use Cache Components ('use cache'), an RCE through librsvg when attacker-supplied SVGs reach sharp (dangerouslyAllowSVG or next/og on Node), and a Server Actions CPU-exhaustion DoS. No exploitation was reported as of Oct 15. Two of the advisories carry no CVE and may not show up in npm audit, so upgrade and redeploy directly, and on v15 confirm sharp is 0.35.5 or later.

items.title: Drupal core Field UI flaw rated critical, with a no-login RCE path through contributed modules
items.summary: Drupal fixed a critical Field UI weakness that core alone does not expose but that contributed modules or custom code can turn into code execution, at least one path needing no authentication. Fixed releases are 11.4.10, 11.3.19 and 10.6.19; end-of-life branches get nothing, and no public exploit had appeared by Oct 15, though the security team expects one quickly. Update core (or uninstall field_ui as a stopgap) and separately update the Entity List module to 3.0.10 for its own critical RCE.

items.title: GhostAction's October burst hit about 1,900 GitHub accounts and pushed secret-stealing workflows at 30,000+ repos
items.summary: GitGuardian says the GhostAction crew used stolen tokens to push fake 'security audit' GitHub Actions workflows (security-audit.yml, github_actions_security.yml) that scrape CI secrets and git history for cloud, registry and AI API keys, with a spike on Oct 8-9. GitHub began blocking the workflow from running on Oct 9, but some victims were repeat targets whose secrets had never been rotated. Search all branches for those workflow files since Aug 31, remove them, rotate every exposed secret and revoke stale personal access tokens.

items.title: NGINX 1.30.6 and 1.31.7 fix three memory bugs and a TLS session flaw that can skip client-cert checks
items.summary: Five NGINX bugs are fixed: two heap overflows and a use-after-free that need specific alias/rewrite, regex map or aio+SSI configurations, an HTTP/3 request-smuggling style issue, and a shared TLS session cache weakness that can let a forged session bypass client-certificate verification. None are reported exploited. Upgrade to 1.30.6 or 1.31.7 (check distro backports and F5 products separately), or run nginx -T and apply F5's per-directive workarounds.

items.title: LiteLLM gateway flaws let low-privilege users reach admin functions and leak AI provider keys
items.summary: Check Point found a missing authorization check in LiteLLM that lets even read-only users change runtime config and get code execution, plus an SSRF that can send requests carrying provider API keys to an attacker's server. Both are fixed in 1.83.9, and no in-the-wild exploitation has been reported. Upgrade, prune gateway accounts, test that limited roles really are limited, and rotate stored provider keys if you suspect earlier abuse.

items.title: HiddenLayer shows 'decision model' browser agents still fall for indirect prompt injection
items.summary: HiddenLayer built a mock shop where a browser agent on TypeSafe AI's Jev was told to buy the cart unchanged, and a fake sponsored 'Confirm Price' button still hijacked it; a tuned Qwen model failed the same way, more often. A character-padding trick also slipped toxic prompts past Jev used as a verifier. The lesson: a system-prompt rule to distrust page content is not a control, so put independent checks in front of any agent action with real consequences.

items.title: Censys: internet-exposed AI software up 63% in nine months, led by vulnerable n8n instances
items.summary: Censys counted about 268,000 exposed hosts running AI-related software across 44 products in July 2026, up from about 164,000 in October 2025. n8n accounts for roughly 114,000 of them, and about three quarters of those reporting a version run a release with at least one 9.0+ CVE; self-hosted OpenClaw agent panels also climbed into the tens of thousands. Inventory your own AI tooling, keep admin and workflow panels off the public internet, and patch them like any other edge service.
